panels.visual: A roadside house on the road to Athens at dusk, an iron bed, and a grinning huge host Procrustes inviting a traveller in
panels.caption: On the road to Athens lived a man called Procrustes. He offered travellers a bed for the night.

panels.visual: A lanky traveller lying on a short iron bed with his feet hanging off and Procrustes looming with a mallet, a sweat drop
panels.caption: If a guest was too short, he stretched him. If too tall, he chopped off his legs.

panels.visual: Procrustes, a hulking grinning villain with an axe, looms over his iron bed in a dark room; the young hero Theseus in the lit doorway in silhouette, sword in hand, long shadow; no blood
panels.caption: Then Theseus came down the road.

panels.visual: A quiet empty road at sunrise with the iron bed abandoned and Theseus walking away, tiny
panels.caption: We still say a Procrustean bed: forcing everything to fit one rule.
